3,791 likes, 23 comments - ranveer.brar on October 8, 2026: "We have long since established the scientific logic behind our socio-religious practices, both at the spiritual and culinary levels. This includes seasonal changes in food patterns, as well as fasting.

Fasting, or vrat, in its varying degrees, from complete to partial abstinence, is an essential detox for our digestive system.

Take Navratri, for instance. There are two major Navratris in a year (four in all), both occurring during major seasonal shifts: the beginning of spring and autumn. These are also times when human immunity is believed to be at its lowest. Eating light and avoiding rich, heavy, and spicy foods helps the body adjust to the new season naturally.

That brings us to the importance of eating right during fasts. Getting plenty of energy and fibre-rich foods while staying hydrated is the order of the day. Hence, the inclusion of millets as grain substitutes is no surprise, considering they were an Indian staple in days of yore.

And it’s not just Navratri that highlights the significance of fasting. Similar beliefs surround Ekadashi, the 11th day in the lunar cycle. The concept is simple: eating light puts less pressure on the digestive process, helping the senses stay alert and active.

So this season, while you observe fasts and enjoy the feasts, don’t forget to honour what your body truly needs.

#ranveerbrar #navratri #durgapuja #navratrifast #upvasrecipe".

80K likes, 205 comments - ranveer.brar on October 7, 2026: "My journey with Nana Patekar began with Parinda. I was struck by the raw intensity he brought to every scene—and that feeling stayed with me. Then came Prahaar, Krantiveer, and Ab Tak Chhappan, each revealing a new layer of an extraordinary actor.

But Natsamrat touched something deeper. Watching him as Ganpat Belwalkar—a man who had once commanded the stage but could no longer hold his family together—was devastating. His pain felt so real that it lingered long after the film ended.

Over time, I began to see the person beyond the performances.
Through Naam Foundation, he stood beside families devastated by farmer suicides, helped revive rivers, and brought water to drought-stricken villages. He did not seek the spotlight for these acts; he simply showed up where people needed help.

He was a man who could command a screen—and, quietly and humbly, help change lives beyond it.

Somewhere along the way, my admiration for the actor deepened into respect for the human being.

Today, as I remember not only the fire and intensity he brought to his performances, but also the compassion, dignity, and humanity he carried beyond the screen.

Rest in peace, Nana Patekar.
.
.
.
.

#RIPNanaPatekar".
